PullRequest.Title: Bump @vscode/markdown-editor to 0.0.2-187
PullRequest.Body:
Updates `@vscode/markdown-editor` in `extensions/markdown-language-features` from `0.0.2-184` to `0.0.2-187` (`microsoft/vscode-packages@6f292f3e`).

## Included `@vscode/markdown-editor` changes
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#477](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/477): render raw HTML through a sanitized allowlist
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#476](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/476): render Setext headings and reference link definitions
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#473](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/473): add `zoomPercent` support (25%–400%)
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#471](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/471): CJK IME EditContext bounds, composition underlines, and comment input guard fixes
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#470](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/470): fix link click in Editing mode, right-aligned table cell hit-testing, and table cell text selection
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#469](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/469): fix backslash escapes, character references, currency `$`, and LaTeX math delimiters
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#451](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/451): clarify read-only toggle state
- [microsoft/vscode-packages#450](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/450): render indented GFM tables like unindented ones

## Validation
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (via `dev-workspace install`)
- `typecheck`, `markdownEditorBuild`, `markdownScriptTests` (18 passing), `markdownExtensionTests` (236 passing)
- `updateMarkdownEditorPackageJson.mts --check` (unchanged) and `hygiene`

Scenarios.Scenario: Install and bundle the updated Markdown editor dependency
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dependency resolution must supply the selected package before esbuild can bundle editor.ts and its CSS. This is build/install work, not a newly added application-startup operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain the selected package artifact on a cold install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changed package artifact; no additional dependency resolutions are introduced by the lockfile diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install operation obtained version 0.0.2-184 instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for installation/build when the selected version is not cached; not on the editor's runtime critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve package exports, read package code/CSS during bundling, and inspect the manifest-generation module timestamp.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing package inputs per build; the optional local override reads one manifest and resolves its real directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical build integration bundled version 0.0.2-184.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to produce the webview bundle, before the application consumes it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pinned package changes from 0.0.2-184 to 0.0.2-187. The lockfile dependency list and all other resolved packages remain unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The unchanged esbuild integration determines build scheduling; the diff adds no loop, process creation, limiter change, or runtime dependency-loading phase.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already cached selected version can be reused; a cold install needs the new artifact. Package sizes and package-manager cache state are unavailable. Runtime uses the bundle rather than resolving the npm package dynamically.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the complete diff changes only the selected package version and integrity, not dependency cardinality or build integration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Neither package artifact size nor the upstream implementation differences are available through the supplied repository tools.
Scenarios.Verdict: No concrete build or installation performance regression is established by the version replacement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, render, scroll, and edit Markdown, including raw HTML, headings, tables, math, IME input, and comments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host generates initial-state HTML, the browser loads editor.js/editor.css, and Editor constructs EditorModel and EditorView with initial text. Model/view work is on the webview UI thread. Host content synchronization follows connection; the initial view does not wait for contributed editor descriptors.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify and URI-encode initial document content and configuration into webview HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial-state encoding per webview generation, proportional to document bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial content encoding and HTML generation occurred with the previous dependency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the webview's initial editor can be constructed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The webview loads the existing editor.js and editor.css bundle resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same two entry resources per webview load, subject to browser caching; upstream bundle size changes are unknown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The webview loaded the same bundle entry paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exchange content edits and selection messages with the extension host and apply workspace edits to the authoritative document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing content-update messages; selection reports are coalesced within a microtask and multi-step writes are coalesced for content synchronization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same WebEditorClient, RPC transport, edit application, and coalescing paths were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local initial rendering precedes host readiness; authoritative edits and native undo depend on host synchronization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document bytes, rendered blocks, table cells, HTML content, comments, and input/scroll frequency. The published editor's effective rendering and IME work cardinality cannot be inspected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model/view creation and local event handlers execute on the browser UI thread; host communication is asynchronous. Selection reporting is microtask-coalesced. No integration scheduling or ownership change appears in this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial text is serialized once per webview generation. Existing content listeners avoid setting text when it already matches. The comment input controller is created only while comments are accepted and disposed when that scope ends. Upstream parser/render caches are unavailable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: The integration critical path, serialization, and disposal ownership are directly visible. There is insufficient evidence about changed EditorModel/EditorView implementation to establish an introduced costly mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new and old published package implementations are not present in the readable repository; an attempted installed-package read failed. The PR description's feature summaries are not implementation evidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence finding. This is a meaningful limitation: internal rendering, HTML sanitization, zoom, and IME performance changes cannot be compared from this dependency-only diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display and update syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: HighlighterDocument renders an unstyled or previous snapshot immediately, then asynchronously requests themed tokens. Tokenization runs in the workbench after IPC and its completion is required for the final highlighted result, not the initial text display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send full code-block source through webview RPC and extension-host/workbench RPC; return token and color-map data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing highlighter create/update/refresh, not per token; payload scales with block source and returned tokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same adapter and proposed API performed these requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous with an immediate fallback snapshot; final syntax colors await the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a tokenizer and tokenize every line of the supplied code-block source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-source tokenization per issued request; line processing is serial within each request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical full-source tokenization implementation was reached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks workbench execution while tokenizing and delays the highlight response, but the diff does not change the implementation or prove more requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Code-block source bytes and lines, number of highlighter sessions created by EditorView, edits to those sessions, and theme refreshes. Upstream changes to session creation frequency are unavailable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each create/update/refresh issues an asynchronous request without an adapter-wide limiter. mainThreadLanguages tokenizes all source lines synchronously once its tokenizer is available. No change to this scheduling is visible.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The adapter retains tokens per live session and removes disposed sessions. It does not cache request results or debounce requests; version checks discard stale results after issuance. These behaviors are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the existing source-transfer and tokenization mechanism; no evidence that the bumped package increases request cardinality or makes it newly synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session counts and reconstruction frequency inside either package version cannot be determined; tokenization durations are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Existing full-block tokenization is not reportable without evidence that this diff increases its work or frequency.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial Markdown view is constructed without waiting for provider descriptor loading. Static providers are read in the background. The adapter module loads only after create is called with providers present; embedded editor initialization waits for its descriptor and module.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read static provider HTML, or URI-backed resolved provider HTML, and UTF-8 decode it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per static provider per load; one URI read per cold successful descriptor key when the provider returns URI content. Inline HTML requires no read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider loop, reads, and descriptor caching existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that embedded editor's availability, not initial Markdown view creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve contributed editor descriptors over webview RPC and activate/access extension provider APIs; exchange runtime host-transport messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Descriptor work is coalesced by distinct provider/document/language key; activation is cached per provider; runtime message count depends on live embedded editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC routes, activation cache, and transport ownership applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Embedded editor availability depends on resolution; plain Markdown rendering does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the bundled @vscode/markdown-editor/web-editors chunk on first embedded-editor demand.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one load attempt per lazy factory instance, with browser module caching across uses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lazy dynamic import was used for the prior package.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for embedded-editor creation, not plain document startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Static provider count and distinct provider/document-URI/language combinations, rather than one descriptor filesystem read per code block. Runtime iframe/transport counts are controlled by the unavailable virtualized factory implementation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Static descriptor reads are serial within the provider-loading loop. Different resolution keys may proceed concurrently; requests for the same key join its promise. No new global burst or loss of laziness is visible.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The lazy factory starts one module load per factory instance. API activation promises are cached per provider. Descriptor promises coalesce by provider/document/language; successful results remain cached, while undefined/failed results are evicted and can retry. Provider changes clear resolution caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in integration grouping, serial static reads, per-key joining, and lazy module loading. No upstream virtualized-factory changes can be established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider counts, descriptor sizes, embedded-runtime cardinality, and upstream virtualization behavior are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No evidence that this dependency bump defeats existing laziness, coalescing, or cache ownership; unchanged costs are out of scope.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve rich links and open links from reading or editing mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rich-link presentations initially show loading state and resolve asynchronously. Link clicks first await sync.drain, then any contributed opener, link resolution, and the final open/reveal command. Workspace and Git metadata are not prerequisites for initial document rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Batch webview subscription changes, create/dispose presentation watchers across extension-host/workbench boundaries, and publish presentation updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched subscription notification per microtask; watchers are per distinct active href and underlying built-in resolver work is shared by canonical href.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same batching, watcher routes, reference counting, and shared service existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous presentation enhancement, off the initial render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat a workspace resource for its rich-link presentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per distinct shared active workspace href per resolution/refresh, not per duplicate link occurrence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stat and 30-second/event refresh behavior applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git show -s --shortstat for a commit; path-hinted lookups can also discover/open a repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git-show process per matching repository for each cold uncached commit href, or one for a path-hinted repository. Successful hrefs are cached; failures can repeat. Direct clicks perform lookup separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache, repository filtering, parallel lookups, and spawn path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async for presentation; opening a commit waits for lookup and git.viewCommit. Promise.allSettled waits for all candidate repository results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve local/relative link targets using a language-client request and invoke open/reveal commands; absolute non-file targets bypass language-service resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution request for each applicable click or newly watched relative href; no request for absolute non-file target resolution. Click work follows synchronization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same drain, link resolution, and command paths existed; the package's changed click handling is unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-requested navigation awaits resolution and opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct active hrefs per webview, deduplicated canonical hrefs in the shared presentation service, and matching repositories for each cold Git commit href. Click work scales with user clicks, not all document links.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Distinct hrefs resolve asynchronously. Git lookups without a path hint use Promise.allSettled across matching repositories and directly reach spawning without a global limiter on this path. Same successful commit hrefs share a promise. Workspace refresh runs every 30 seconds while relevant watches exist. Link click steps are awaited in order.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Webview entries are reference-counted by href and subscription changes are microtask-batched; inactive entries are limited to 256 and five minutes. The shared service groups canonical hrefs across watchers. Successful immutable Git presentations and Git API activation are cached; rejected commit lookups evict their entry. Workspace presentations stat again on refresh/events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in visible href deduplication, cache states, effective Git subprocess cardinality, and click ordering. No evidence ties a change in those counts to the version bump.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The package's changed rendering of reference links/raw HTML may alter link creation, but the implementation and actual added watcher cardinality are unavailable. Third-party presentation-provider internals and timings are also unavailable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced fan-out or retention mechanism can be proven. Existing per-distinct-href and per-matching-repository work is not a finding on this PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass after reading the entire two-file inventory and all four diff hunks. The PR only replaces a pinned package version and its lockfile integrity/key; transitive dependencies and repository integration code do not change. Traced startup/rendering, input, highlighting, embedded editors, and rich-link/navigation boundaries and compared visible before/after scheduling, grouping, caching, and ownership. No high-confidence diff-caused performance issue or concrete regression fix was established. Main limitation: neither published package implementation was available through the supplied read-only tools, so upstream changes could not be reviewed directly. The requested guide tool response was truncated by the host; the learned-mechanism document and supplied focus instructions were available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
